newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan says 1996 debt seen at 90 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says 1996 debt seen at 90 pct of GDP.

text.p: Jordan's foreign debt stood at $6.495 billion, or 90 percent of GDP, at the end of October 1996, the finance minister said on Wednesday.
Marwan Awad said in a speech on the 1997 draft budget that better management helped cut foreign debt from a high of 190 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1990.

"The debt has been reduced due to the growth in GDP and conservative management of debt and policies to reduce the debt by debt buy-back, restructuring, dependance on borrowing on easy terms and some write-offs of foreign debts," he said.
Awad said Jordan would repay $582 million in interest and principal in 1996 following rescheduling accords over the last few years with major creditor nations.

Jordan embarked on an International Monetary Fund (IMF) reform package after an economic crisis in 1989 totally wiped out foreign reserves. It has since achieved fiscal and monetary stability and cut its budget deficit to around 4.6 percent of GDP in 1996 from a high 24 percent 1990.
The draft 1997 budget of 1.92 billion dinars ($2.7 billion) reflects accelerated IMF reforms in 1997-1998 aimed at further liberalising the economy. ($=0.7080 dinar)
